name: bucket
title: Bucket
description: The documents in a folder of your S3 bucket. Each file is read whole and placed on the map by the needs it answers.

files.config.yaml:
# WHAT A PERSON SETS TO RUN THIS PIPELINE: the Import form, rendered by the canvas the way a
# node's config is. Only what the collect step does not know by itself: which bucket, which
# folder. The credential is the node's, found by type in the org's store.
configSchema:
  type: object
  required: [bucket]
  properties:
    bucket:
      type: string
      title: Bucket
      description: The S3 bucket your documents are uploaded to.
      default: ""
      # AN S3 BUCKET NAME: 3 to 63 lowercase letters, digits, dots and hyphens, starting and ending
      # with a letter or digit. A path pasted here ("my-bucket/folder/") is refused before the run.
      pattern: "^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9.-]{1,61}[a-z0-9]$"
      placeholder: acme-documents
    prefix:
      type: string
      title: Folder
      description: The folder in the bucket to read. Ends with a slash. Leave blank for the whole bucket.
      default: ""
      placeholder: guides/
"ui:order": [bucket, prefix]
files.interface.yaml:
# A PIPELINE ON A CANVAS, as a node: the folder may be named by an upstream node instead of
# the form, and its rows go downstream. The collect step's node carries its own credential,
# so this declares none.
inputs:
  - name: signal
    type: object
    description: The folder to read, as { bucket, prefix }, when wired from an upstream node instead of the form
    required: false

outputs:
  - name: rows
    type: array
    description: The inbox rows this run collected, one per file, held until they are run
  - name: total
    type: number
    description: How many rows this run collected

credentials: []
files.pipeline.yaml:
unoverse: "1.0"
# A PIPELINE IS THE SOURCE SIDE: how content is collected and which objects it may yield.
# It never knows how an object is built; that is the object's own api/service.yaml. Between
# collect and the map sit the platform's steps, the same for every pipeline and every
# object: known, understand, make detail, match, retire, save (docs/unoverse/data/pipelines/README.md).
# A pipeline fills the collect slot and names its yields. It adds no step of its own.
type: pipeline
name: bucket

# THE FACE, as a node's node.yaml carries it.
title: Bucket
description: >-
  The documents in a folder of your S3 bucket. Each file is read whole and placed on the map
  by the needs it answers.
whenToUse: >-
  Bring a folder of documents onto the map: guides, reports, policies, whatever the business
  has written at length, uploaded to one folder in your bucket. Give it the bucket and the
  folder. One file is one document. Every file lands in the inbox, held, until you run it.
category: Pipelines
version: 1.0.0
color: "#FF9900"
logoUrl: https://res.cloudinary.com/sonik/image/upload/v1749916163/gravity/icons/Amazon-S3-Logo.svg.png

# COLLECT: the folder's listing, and only that. The node carries the org's AWS credential,
# found by type; nothing is repeated here. Links are not minted here: the document's own
# makeDetail mints one when it parses.
collect:
  - name: files
    node: S3Files
    config:
      bucket: "{{ config.bucket }}"
      prefix: "{{ config.prefix }}"
      fileExtensions: [pdf, docx, pptx, xlsx, xlsm, md, txt]
      maxKeys: 1000

# ONE ROW PER FILE (owner ruling 2026-09-09), the bucket captured on it. The source is the
# file's own address, which is what the document's makeDetail reads the bucket and key off
# and what match and retire are scoped to; the source id is the listing's stable id, which
# changes when the file is replaced. The content is thin on purpose: the file's name and
# where it is, enough for the row's record; the whole read is the document's own.
# `_parsed/` is the reserved name for parsed output at any depth (owner ruling 2026-09-09
# evening): never a document; every other subfolder is read.

# WHAT THIS PIPELINE MAKES: one document per file, parsed by the document's own function;
# then the needs each document speaks to, read from the document's text, never the file
# again. `_parsed/` is reserved at any depth and never read as a source.
make:
  # EACH FILE becomes one document, read from its first two pages and its headings; its tables
  # and meaningful figures are rows of their own, off the map.
  - each: "{{ collect.files.files }}"
    document:
      cardinality: one
      parts:
        table: "{{ detail.tables }}"
        figure: "{{ detail.figures }}"
files.test.yaml:
# THE PIPELINE UNDER GUARD: the collect step faked with a fixture listing, the rows it
# yields asserted. Two files in, two inbox rows out, each addressed by its own s3 address,
# identified by the listing's stable id, carrying the file as listed, stamped with this
# pipeline's yields. What a row becomes is the document object's own test.
testData:
  config:
    bucket: example-docs
    prefix: guides/
  fake:
    files:
      count: 2
      files:
        - { key: guides/onboarding.pdf, name: onboarding.pdf, size: 812345, bucket: example-docs, address: "s3://example-docs/guides/onboarding.pdf", universalId: 3f1a9c2b7d4e }
        - { key: guides/fees.docx, name: fees.docx, size: 91234, bucket: example-docs, address: "s3://example-docs/guides/fees.docx", universalId: 9b8c7d6e5f4a }
  expect:
    rows: "return output.rows.length === 2"
    source: "return output.rows[0].sourceUrl === 's3://example-docs/guides/onboarding.pdf' && output.rows[1].sourceUrl === 's3://example-docs/guides/fees.docx'"
    identity: "return output.rows[0].sourceId === '3f1a9c2b7d4e'"
    content: "return output.rows[0].content.name === 'onboarding.pdf' && output.rows[0].content.bucket === 'example-docs' && output.rows[0].content.key === 'guides/onboarding.pdf' && output.rows[0].content.size === 812345"
    yields: "return output.rows.every(r => r.yields.join(',') === 'document')"
    parsed: "return output.rows.every(r => !r.content.key.includes('_parsed'))"
